newsitem.title: USA: Corp issuers creep out of woodwork amid rate dip.
newsitem.headline: Corp issuers creep out of woodwork amid rate dip.

text.p: While a dip in interest rates triggered a few high-grade issuers to creep out of the woodwork, the bulk of this week's supply is slated to come from the junk arena, dealers said.

"The tone is a little upbeat but we're still not where we were a week and a half ago," said one high-grade syndicate source. "If this continues, we may see some more names but for now its just wait and see."
Currently, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 17/32 at 97-3/32 to yield 6.60 percent.
On July 31, the yield on the T-bond closed at 6.30 percent. Since then, rising long-term interest rates have sidelined the more rate sensitive investment grade issuers.
Meanwhile, among the new high-grade names that have emerged is Texas Utilities. The issuer is expected to sell $300 million in Baa2/BBB 10-year debt via Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, sources said.
Another issuer, ServiceMaster Co LP is expected to issue a $300 million two-part debt offering via JP Morgan Securities.

S&P said the downgrade was based on the firm's higher debt levels following the completion of the Barefoot Inc acquisition for $232 million and the repurchase of WMX Technologies' ownership interest in ServiceMaster.
ServiceMaster provides management of housekeeping, plant operations, food, linen and other services to healthcare and educational facilities.
Among other expected issues is a $125 million 10-year A3/A rated debt offering from Martin Marietta Materials' via Goldman Sachs & Co, syndicate players said.
